ThingDef.label: Type 56C
ThingDef.description:
Caliber: 7.62x39mm. 30-round detachable mag. Select-Fire.
The Type 56 is a Chinese copy of the Soviet Avtomat Kalashnikov (AK) rifle. Though almost a 1:1 copy of the Type III AK, the Type 56 has some notable differences - notably, most are found with stamped (like on the AKM) rather than milled receivers, and the Type 56 has a distinctive enclosed hooded front sight. Type 56 rifles also often feature their own integral folding bayonets (though this rifle does not have one, instead using a typical AKM-style bayonet.) Chinese AKs are among the most common in the world today, Type 56 rifles in their original configuration are still produced.
This variant is a Type 56C, a modification created in the early 1990s that was designed to be more compact and portable while still offering the firepower of the 7.62 caliber round. The Type 56C notably breaks from older variants by featuring polymer furniture, using a variation of the folding stock from the Type 56-2, and featuring a shorter barrel that gives it a slight resemblance to the Soviet AKS-74U which was designed for a similar purpose. Type 56Cs only saw limited use in China itself, as the AK platform had long been superceded by the Type 81 and the country was in the process of adopting the 5.8mm round.
